The '''2017–18 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 116th season of top-tier Italian [[Association football|football]], the 86th in a [[round-robin tournament]] and the 8th since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] were the six-time defending champions. The season ran from 19 August 2017 to 20 May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/104026/serie-schedule-announced|title=Serie A schedule announced - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/2017/06/12/news/stagione_2017_18_ecco_tutte_le_date_serie_a_senza_sosta_a_natale_supercoppa_il_13_agosto-167941774/|title=All dates of 2017/18 season: no stop for Xmas, Super Cup on August 13|website=repubblica.it|date=12 June 2017|language=it}}</ref>

On 13 May, Juventus won a record seventh consecutive title and 34th title overall with one game remaining following their 0–0 draw with [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44103089 |title=Roma 0–0 Juventus|date=13 May 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 May 2018}}</ref>

The season was marred by the death of [[Davide Astori]], the captain of [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], due to heart problems.

==Events==
On 13 May 2017, [[S.P.A.L.|SPAL]] were mathematically promoted from [[2016–17 Serie B|Serie B]] after 49 years away.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calciomercato.com/news/serie-b-live-61086|title=SERIE B: LA SPAL PERDE MA TORNA IN SERIE A DOPO 49 ANNI!}}</ref> Five days later, [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] clinched promoted as well, one year on from being relegated. On 8 June 2017, [[Benevento Calcio|Benevento]] won the promotion play-offs to earn the club a first ever promotion to Serie A; they became the 67th team to participate in the Italian top flight.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/103864/serie-benvenuto-benevento|title=Serie A: Benvenuto, Benevento! - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref>

After [[video assistant referee]]ing (VAR) was privately tested in the [[2016–17 Serie A|previous season]], on 10 June 2017 it was announced replay assistance would be implemented for this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/103940/serie-will-start-var|title=Serie A will start with VAR|publisher=Football Italia|date=10 June 2017|access-date=10 June 2017}}</ref> The percentage of errors in Serie A in this season was reportedly 0.89 percent, compared to 5.78 percent if VAR had not been not used.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/122668/var-stats-show-revolution|title=VAR stats show revolution|publisher=Football Italia|date=8 June 2018}}</ref>

Subsequently to the new UEFA entry criteria, Italy obtained four group stage spots for the following [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] season, as did the other three leagues with the highest [[UEFA coefficient|coefficient]] in Europe; this was an improvement on the three Champions League spots (two group stage places and one qualifying play-off place) that Serie A had received prior.

On 4 March 2018, [[Davide Astori]], captain of [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], died in his sleep while staying in a hotel in [[Udine]] prior to Fiorentina's match against [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]], proven to be caused by [[cardiac arrest]] determined from an [[autopsy]] conducted two days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/118132/confirmed-astori-died-cardiac-arrest|title=Confirmed: Astori died of cardiac arrest|publisher=Football Italia|date=6 March 2018}}</ref> All [[Serie A]], [[Serie B]] and [[Serie C]] matches scheduled for 4 March were postponed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/118048/official-serie-games-cancelled|title=Official: Serie A games cancelled|publisher=Football Italia|date=4 March 2018}}</ref> Cagliari and Fiorentina both [[List of retired numbers in association football#Retired numbers|retired]] the [[Squad number (association football)|number 13 jersey]] worn by Astori in his honour.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/118117/astori-shirt-retired|title=Astori shirt retired|publisher=Football Italia|date=6 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43300633|title=Davide Astori: Fiorentina and Cagliari retire defender's number 13 shirt|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 March 2018|access-date=6 March 2018}}</ref>

The teams that were relegated included [[Benevento Calcio|Benevento]] (on 22 April 2018, after one year in Serie A),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/120310/benevento-relegated-serie-b|title=Benevento relegated to Serie B {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|access-date=23 April 2018}}</ref> [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] (on 5 May 2018, also after one year),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calciomercato.com/news/milan-verona-live-92775|title=Milan-Verona LIVE}}</ref> and [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]] (on 20 May 2018, after two seasons in the top flight).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/serie-a-la-classifica-aggiornata-crotone-in-b-napoli-record-di-punti-1113717|title=Serie A, la classifica aggiornata: Crotone in B. Napoli, record di punti - TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|website=www.tuttomercatoweb.com}}</ref>

On 13 May 2018, [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] won their seventh title in a row and the 34th in their history following their 0–0 draw away to [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] in the penultimate matchweek.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/121329/juventus-seven|title=Juventus Seven-Up {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|date=13 May 2018|access-date=17 May 2018}}</ref> Four days later, Juventus goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Buffon]] announced his farewell to [[Serie A]] (and the [[Italy national football team|national football team]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/juventus/?action=read&idtmw=1112556|title=TMW News - Buffon, l\'addio alla Juve e le riflessioni in corso}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/juventus/?action=read&idnet=dHV0dG9qdXZlLmNvbS00MjIxMDU|title=LIVE TJ - BUFFON: "Non è certo che smetterò di giocare. Capitolo chiuso con la Nazionale. Dispiaciuto per le esternazioni dopo Madrid"}}</ref> He left the league after 23 career seasons, the last seventeen being with Juventus, having earned nine league titles and 640 caps, the second highest ever in Serie A.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.calciomercato.com/news/buffon-nella-leggenda-dal-parma-a-juve-e-nazionale-tutti-i-recor-94715|title=Buffon nella leggenda: dal Parma a Juve e Nazionale, tutti i record}}</ref> However, after a year away with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], Buffon would return to Juventus and to Serie A for the [[2019–20 Serie A|2019–20]] season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48873137|title=Gianluigi Buffon returns to Juventus after one season at Paris St-Germain|date=4 July 2019|access-date=4 July 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>
